clue.text: Residue of apple and spice added to reduced-size pot

indicators.note: the spice is tacked on after the trimmed pot
a pot cut down in size loses its final letter here

parts.note: the word pot itself, before trimming
mace is a spice made from the husk of nutmeg

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: put apple residue and spice into a smaller pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced-size' cuts the T from POT, leaving PO, and MACE is 'added to' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomace is the pulp left after apples are pressed for cider, a residue.

clue.text: Lawman put pressure on family involved in crime

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: the family is caught up inside the crime

parts.note: arson is the crime of fire-raising
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A police officer leans on a family mixed up in wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawman' suggests a sheriff; it is C. Northcote Parkinson, whose law says work expands to fill the time available.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkinson formulated Parkinson's Law, so he is a man known for a law.

clue.text: In Massachusetts, "key" is an island

indicators.note: the key goes in the state's abbreviation

parts.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: In Massachusetts a certain word means an island, quotation marks and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a Florida-style islet; it is the Alt key.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Restrict wild animals in parts of America

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose

explanation.surface: An instruction to confine wild animals in American regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks like it describes the animals; it signals rearranging RESTRICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Critters is American dialect for creatures, especially animals.

clue.text: Problems in book with small cover wrapped round

indicators.note: the cover is wrapped around the book, so it goes outside
turned round, so the small-plus-cover pair is read backwards

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small (clothing sizes)
a lid is a cover
Emma is Jane Austen's novel

explanation.surface: Difficulties found in a book that has a little cover wrapped around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reverses the small cover to give DILS, which is 'wrapped' about the Austen title.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilemmas are awkward choices, so they are problems in the everyday sense.

clue.text: As a result, popular party game hasn't succeeded

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: has not means is without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Consequences is a parlour game of folded paper stories
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Therefore a fashionable party game proved unsuccessful.
explanation.walkthrough: Consequences is a British parlour game in which players write story lines on paper folded over each turn; 'hasn't' drops its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as a consequence, thus or as a result.

clue.text: News chief travelled up carrying computers etc

indicators.note: the travelling word carries the computing letters inside it
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: rode means travelled on horse or vehicle
IT, information technology

explanation.surface: The head of a newsroom went upstairs with the office computers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives EDOR; 'carrying' holds the computing letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is the person in charge of a newspaper, its head of news.

clue.text: Philosopher, one engaged by queen over many years

parts.note: John Stuart Mill, the English philosopher

indicators.note: taken on inside, so one goes into the queen
in a down clue over means turned upside down, reversed

parts.note: Queen Anne of Great Britain
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A philosopher and a single individual taken on by a queen for a long stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ANNE into ENNA, and 'engaged by' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Millennia are thousands of years, so very many years.

clue.text: A small amount of extremely smooth wine

indicators.note: at the extremes, so the first and last letters of smooth

parts.note: red is a wine

explanation.surface: A sip of very smooth wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a scrap or tiny bit of something.

clue.text: Courtier just wasting time drinking beer

indicators.note: the trimmed word takes in the beer, so it surrounds it
wasting means losing, so the time letter drops out

parts.note: just as in fair, right
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A courtier fritters away his time in drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' leaves RIGH, and 'drinking' takes the beer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was a favourite courtier of Elizabeth I.

clue.text: A detective, I report louche suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are unsound and rearranged

explanation.surface: An investigator reports that a seedy character is a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like a noun in a detective story; it signals rearranging I REPORT LOUCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's Belgian sleuth is one of fiction's best-known detectives.

clue.text: Author wanting introduction for scary book

indicators.note: lacking its opening letter, so the first letter of the author goes

parts.note: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and playwright

explanation.surface: A writer lacking an opening chapter for his horror novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting introduction' drops the S from SCHILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiller is a frightening story or film, a horror tale.

clue.text: To fall asleep during sex is ….

definitions.text: To fall asleep during sex is ….

indicators.note: during places the dozing inside the sex

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal
to nap is to drop off briefly

explanation.surface: Nodding off in the middle of lovemaking is, the clue tails off, rather unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis invites the solver to finish the sentence: the whole clue defines and builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, which dozing off mid-sex would be.

clue.text: Declined to look into S African capital

indicators.note: the looking phrase goes inside the currency

parts.note: capital as in money: the rand is South Africa's currency
to see is to look

explanation.surface: Someone refused to investigate the capital city of South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' tempts a city such as Pretoria; it is money, the currency, which 'into' opens to take the looking phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To run to seed is to deteriorate, so declined is the past form of that idiom.

clue.text: Great drink, um … ah … wolfing dessert back

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: wolfing is eating greedily, so the hesitations swallow the dessert

parts.note: two hesitations, each written ER

indicators.note: back means the dessert is read in reverse

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A hesitant diner calls the drink great while gobbling the pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives DUP, which 'wolfing' sets between the two hesitations.
explanation.definitionFit: Super-duper is a jokey intensified form of super, meaning excellent.

clue.text: Cut up tat for trouser material

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a snip is a cut
both mean rubbish, worthless stuff

explanation.surface: Chop up some cheap junk to make fabric for trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SNIP into PINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripe is the fabric with fine stripes used for business suits and trousers.

clue.text: Probably had read Steinbeck's last novel

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the novelist's surname

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: Someone has probably read the last book John Steinbeck wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun after Steinbeck; it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Having read something, you probably were aware of it, which is to have been acquainted with it.

clue.text: Ingredient of bread we'll eat hot at dinner, say

indicators.note: will eat means will take inside, so we swallows the letter

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
dinner is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: A baker promises the bread will be eaten warm at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction does double duty: 'we' supplies letters and ''ll eat' tells them to swallow the hot letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheatmeal is flour from wheat, used as an ingredient in brown bread.

clue.text: Firm making explosive, perhaps, quoted for naval admiral

indicators.note: quoted means spoken, so the firm's name is heard

parts.note: jelly is slang for gelignite, an explosive, and CO is company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company making explosives is said to be the source for a naval commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellicoe commanded the British Grand Fleet at Jutland in 1916; 'jelly' is slang for gelignite.
explanation.definitionFit: John Jellicoe was a British admiral of the First World War.

clue.text: Older relative's articles for retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the articles are read in reverse

parts.note: two indefinite articles, an and an

explanation.surface: Granny's belongings set aside for when she retires.
explanation.definitionFit: Nana is a familiar name for a grandmother, an older relation.

clue.text: Recover speed after useless start in park and gym

indicators.note: the speed comes after the other pieces

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a public park

indicators.note: the start of the word useless is its opening letter

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
rate is a speed

explanation.surface: A runner gets back to speed after a poor start training in park and gym.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is a British recreation ground; 'start' takes just the first letter of useless, and 'after' puts the speed last.
explanation.definitionFit: To recuperate is to get well again, to recover from illness or effort.

clue.text: Deal with unruly hair thus, OK?

definitions.meaning: one way to tame wild hair is to give it a permanent wave

explanation.surface: A hairdresser asks whether a permanent wave is the answer to unruly hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words: perm it.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to allow, the verb sense of okay.

clue.text: Moving, tho' not new film

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them

explanation.surface: A film described as moving, though not a recent one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like praise of the film; it signals rearranging THO NOT NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Town is the 1949 Gene Kelly and Frank Sinatra musical film.

clue.text: Watering hole regularly serving locals first

indicators.note: taking every other letter at a regular interval

explanation.surface: A pub that serves its regular locals before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watering hole' suggests a pub; it is the desert spring.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert with water, a literal watering hole.

clue.text: All right to scarper

definitions.meaning: slang for genuine or above board
to run away, as two words: use one's legs

explanation.surface: Fine to make a run for it.
explanation.definitionFit: As one word it is slang for lawful or fine; split, leg it means run off.

clue.text: Exam mark, we'd argue, should be raised a bit

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters run upwards, reversed
a bit of the phrase, letters taken from inside it

explanation.surface: A student argues that their test score ought to go up a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' takes EDARG from inside WE'D ARGUE; 'should be raised' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade is a mark awarded for exam work.

clue.text: Cook limits lunches at first for dieter

indicators.note: to limit is to bound, so the cooking word encloses the letter

parts.note: to simmer is to cook gently

indicators.note: the opening letter of lunches

explanation.surface: A chef restricts lunch portions to help someone on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' puts L inside SIMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimmer is a person trying to lose weight, someone on a diet.

clue.text: Some land in Valence for redevelopment

indicators.note: developing anew means rebuilding, so the town's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plot in the French town of Valence earmarked for property development.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a piece of territory surrounded by another's, a patch of land.

clue.text: Watch muscle is in condition

indicators.note: the muscle sits inside the condition word

parts.note: a state is a condition
pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on whether a muscle is in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' sets the chest muscle inside the condition word.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to look on at an event, to watch it.

clue.text: Unlimited free produce from cattle show

indicators.note: without its limits, the word free loses its outside letters

parts.note: veal is calf meat, something cattle yield

explanation.surface: Free meat on offer at an agricultural cattle show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like a noun, a cattle show; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to disclose or display, so show in the verb sense.
